articles.title: 'Play according to the situation': Aaryavir Sehwag reveals Virat Kohli inspiration after finishing as U19 Asia Cup's top run-scorer
articles.summary: Carrying the Sehwag surname comes with its own expectations, but young India batter Aaryavir Sehwag is keen to carve out his identity by focusing on what
articles.body: Carrying the Sehwag surname comes with its own expectations, but young India batter Aaryavir Sehwag is keen to carve out his identity by focusing on what the team needs rather than sticking to a particular batting style. The 17-year-old has found inspiration in Virat Kohli, whose ability to adapt to match situations and take responsibility has shaped his own approach to batting.Aaryavir enjoyed a memorable campaign at the ACC Under-19 Asia Cup in Oman, finishing as the tournament's leading run-scorer with 361 runs in five matches. His tally included a century and three half-centuries, performances that earned him the Player of the Tournament award as India lifted their ninth title with a thrilling one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the final.The youngster's ability to adapt to different conditions and build his innings according to the team's requirements stood out throughout the competition. Speaking to JioStar, Aaryavir opened up about his admiration for Kohli and explained why he does not want to be labelled as a particular type of batter.'I am a huge Virat Kohli fan': Aaryavir on his batting philosophyAaryavir said Kohli's approach to batting has inspired him to assess situations carefully and adjust his game according to the team's requirements. Rather than identifying himself as an aggressive stroke-maker or an accumulator, the youngster wants to remain flexible and play according to the demands of the match."I don't label myself as a stroke player or any kind of player. I just want to play according to the situation. As I've said earlier, I am a huge Virat Kohli fan, and I want to do what the team requires and needs at that time. I'm glad that I could play the way I did," he told JioStar.Aaryavir Sehwag recalls challenging conditions during 160-run knock against UAEAaryavir smashed 160 off 168 deliveries, including 17 fours and seven sixes, to help India post 309/7 against the UAE. India eventually secured a 70-run victory to book their place in the semifinals. Reflecting on the innings, the youngster revealed that negotiating the initial seam movement was a key part of his plan. However, the pitch also offered unexpected turn, making batting challenging even after the opening overs."Initially, those 10 to 15 overs have always been a challenge in Oman throughout the Asia Cup. In those first 10 to 15 overs, the plan was to see off the seam movement, and after that, shockingly, there was turn as well in that match against UAE. It was a strange kind of wicket, but I'm glad that I could spend a good amount of time on that wicket and once I got set, I just kept batting, and the runs kept coming," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India boycott trophy ceremony after Pakistan handed Blind Asia Cup title following washout
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A massive controversy erupted on Friday after Pakistan were declared the winners of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026 in Dhaka, despite the
articles.body: MUMBAI: A massive controversy erupted on Friday after Pakistan were declared the winners of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026 in Dhaka, despite the much-anticipated final against India being completely washed out.The match referee, Tamim from Bangladesh, declared Pakistan the champions on the basis of their superior Net Run Rate (NRR) in the league stage. However, the Indian team has disputed the decision, claiming that this clause was never mentioned in the tournament's playing conditions provided to them.India subsequently boycotted the trophy presentation ceremony and rejected the match referee's decision to award the title to Pakistan.India had earlier lost to Pakistan in the league stage in a thrilling last-over encounter."It's completely unfair. It's been raining here in Dhaka since yesterday because of a cyclone. The final was supposed to start at 11:30 am. However, the match didn't start at all. As per match rules, we were at the ground (ABG Sports City ground in Dhaka). However, at 4:15 pm, the match was abandoned due to rain and the match referee declared Pakistan the winner due to a better Net Run Rate in the league stage."This rule was never mentioned to us in the playing conditions provided to us, or mentioned in the meetings of the match referee with the captains a day before the tournament began. As per the playing conditions, if the match had been tied and a Super Over was played and that also remained tied, then the winner being decided on the Net Run Rate rule would've been applicable."Nowhere in the history of cricket has one team been declared the winner despite the final being abandoned without a ball being bowled! Neither the ICC nor the MCC rules have such a rule in place in case the final of a tournament is washed out. It's clear that the laws have been twisted to declare Pakistan the tournament winners. Both the teams should have been declared joint winners, or the final should've been played on a reserve day," Dhiraj Sequeira, manager of the Indian blind team, told TOI from Dhaka."We appealed against the decision to award Pakistan the trophy to the technical committee of the tournament, but they too rejected our appeal, despite two members of the panel being in favour of our appeal. Consequently, we decided to boycott the presentation ceremony, after consulting CABI," Sequeira added."CABI is not too hopeful of getting any 'justice' from the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC), as its president is Pakistan's Syed Sultan Shah, who is also the president/chairman of the Pakistan Blind Cricket Council.""Pakistan made the match referee declare the result in their favour, despite the final being totally washed out? How is this possible? I feel very ashamed about it. It's a dark day in the history of blind cricket. A trophy has been awarded to Pakistan, which they don't deserve to win at all. They should feel ashamed to carry this trophy."The organisers never conveyed this rule to us previously, and neither does such a rule of declaring a tournament winner exist. This is a self-made, last-minute rule. We've not accepted this result. Hence, we boycotted the presentation ceremony. I am completely disappointed."We would've been happy if they had beaten India in the final. We don't care. Winning and losing is always a part of the game. In the league match, they defeated us on the last ball (players from both sides shook hands too). That's fine. It was such a wonderful match. We were very happy about it. We accepted it. If they had played and won, we would have gracefully accepted the result," Mahantesh GK, president of the Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI), told TOI."We (India's men's and women's blind teams) are considering abstaining from playing against Pakistan in global tournaments (for the blind) from now on," he asserted.In a strongly worded statement issued on Friday, CABI condemned the decision to declare Pakistan the sole winners of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026 after the final against India was washed out due to rain.CABI categorically rejected the decision, maintaining that India and Pakistan should be recognised as joint winners.According to CABI, Section 27 of the tournament's technical regulations deals specifically with a tied final, with both sentences referring to that situation. CABI said it raised this interpretation with the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) Technical Committee, which initially agreed to declare both teams joint winners.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Selectors are making a blunder': Krishnamachari Srikkanth questions India's handling of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: Former India captain and chief selector Krishnamachari Srikkanth has launched a strong criticism of the selectors and team management over their handling
articles.body: Former India captain and chief selector Krishnamachari Srikkanth has launched a strong criticism of the selectors and team management over their handling of teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, insisting that the youngster deserves a consistent run in the Indian side. Srikkanth believes the 15-year-old has the potential to become a match-winner across formats and even play a significant role in reviving Test cricket globally.Speaking at the sports event on Friday, Srikkanth said the selectors and team management were making a mistake by not providing Sooryavanshi with enough opportunities.'They are discouraging him': Srikkanth slams selectors over Sooryavanshi's treatmentSrikkanth questioned the decision to pick Sooryavanshi for one match and then leave him out for several games, stressing that the youngster needed sustained opportunities to prove his abilities."What they (selectors and team management) are doing with him is not right. They are not encouraging him; they are discouraging him, which is not done. These guys are making a blunder. They play him for one match, they don't play him for five matches. That's not done. Sad," Srikkanth said at the event.'Test cricket revival happens all over the world': Srikkanth backs Sooryavanshi's potentialGoing a step further, Srikkanth suggested that Sooryavanshi's success in the longest format could generate renewed interest in Test cricket, not just in India but across the cricketing world."If Sooryavanshi clicks in Test cricket, a Test cricket revival happens all over the world, not just for India, all over the world. Today in New Zealand, when he was playing the T20 matches, people came all the way -- a full crowd -- to watch Sooryavanshi bat. Wherever he goes, everybody comes to watch Sooryavanshi bat," he said.He called on the selectors to show faith in the youngster and give him a sustained run instead of making frequent changes to his selection."This boy has done so brilliantly for you -- let him play all the matches. Do you mean to say he is not good enough to play Test or One Day cricket? He is 100 per cent sure to play good One Day cricket. Give him 20 innings, tell him he won't get dropped -- you do whatever you want. That boy will win five to seven matches single-handedly for you."And if he scores in Test cricket, the whole world will start reviving Test cricket everywhere, in any part of the world," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asia Cup Rising Stars: India A crush Nepal by 306 runs after bowling them out for 26
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India A registered a staggering 306-run victory over Nepal in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, producing a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India A registered a staggering 306-run victory over Nepal in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, producing a dominant all-round performance at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha.After posting 332/9 in 50 overs, India A's bowlers delivered a sensational performance to dismiss Nepal for just 26 in 11.3 overs. Nepal's total is the fourth-lowest in List A cricket history.Tilak Varma, Kushagra power India A to 332Batting first, India A recovered from a few early setbacks through a magnificent 206-run partnership between captain Tilak Varma and wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra.Kushagra smashed 117 off 102 deliveries, including 10 fours and five sixes, while Varma scored 107 off 113 balls, hitting six fours and four sixes. Both batters registered centuries to put India A in a commanding position.Suryansh Shedge provided the finishing fireworks with an unbeaten 36 off just 14 balls, featuring four sixes and a boundary, as India A finished on 332/9. For Nepal, Lalit Rajbanshi and Sandeep Lamichhane picked up three wickets each.Rana and Prince trigger historic Nepal collapseNepal's chase never got going as Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav exploited the conditions brilliantly, generating considerable swing and seam movement.Returning from injury, Rana looked in excellent rhythm, striking in the opening over by trapping Arjun Kumal lbw for a duck. Prince then dismissed Deepak Dumre and bowled Basir Ahamad as Nepal slipped to 1-3 inside two overs.The collapse continued as Rana and Prince kept finding breakthroughs. Rana finished with four wickets for 16 runs in six overs, while Prince produced a sensational five-wicket haul, conceding just six runs in five overs.Shahbaz Ahmed claimed the final wicket, stumping Nandan Yadav for 2, as Nepal were bundled out for 26. The result sealed a remarkable 306-run win for India A.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'We didn't have our full-strength team here': Nepal captain Lamichhane after 306-run defeat to India A
articles.summary: Nepal captain Sandeep Lamichhane admitted his side were completely outplayed by India A, while pointing to the absence of several first-choice players as
articles.body: Nepal captain Sandeep Lamichhane admitted his side were completely outplayed by India A, while pointing to the absence of several first-choice players as a challenge ahead of their Asia Cup Rising Stars campaign."We were outplayed today. Credit goes to the way the Indian team carried their momentum. We had a good start with the ball, but they utilised their skills. Credit to Tilak and Kumar for the way they handled the pressure," Lamichhane said after the match.The Nepal skipper also revealed that the team were dealing with availability issues, with several players arriving in Doha on the morning of the match due to the ongoing Nepal Premier League (NPL) back home."We didn't have our full-strength team here. A few of the players arrived this morning. NPL is going on back home. We somehow had to manage and put some new faces for this tournament. It was really a hard task for us to manage everything," he added.Despite the heavy defeat, Lamichhane remained confident about Nepal's prospects in the upcoming matches, insisting that the team understood where they had fallen short."But we all are going in the right direction. We are still fully confident about how we're going to approach the upcoming games. We know where we lacked today," he said, reiterating that India A deserved full credit for their performance.Rana, Prince Yadav dismantle Nepal for 26India A’s pace duo of Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav produced a sensational bowling performance to bundle out Nepal for just 26 in 11.3 overs, sealing a massive 306-run victory in their opening match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars 50-over tournament on Friday.Chasing a daunting target of 333, Nepal’s innings fell apart from the outset. Rana struck in the third ball, trapping Arjun Kamal leg-before without scoring, and the wickets continued to tumble. Nepal were reduced to 17 for five by the seventh over as the Indian pacers exploited the pace and swing on offer.Rana finished with impressive figures of 4/16, while Prince was even more devastating, claiming 5/6. The pair accounted for nine of Nepal’s 10 wickets, leaving India A skipper Tilak Varma with no need to use his other bowling options.Left-arm spinner Shahbaz Ahmed picked up the remaining wicket. Nepal’s batting collapse was complete when they were bowled out for 26, with none of their batters managing to reach double figures.Earlier, centuries from Varma (107) and Kumar Kushagra (117) had powered India A to 332 for nine.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India A create history with biggest List A victory by runs, hammer Nepal by 306 runs in Rising Stars Asia Cup
articles.summary: India A produced a record-breaking performance in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, thrashing Nepal by 306 runs at the West
articles.body: India A produced a record-breaking performance in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, thrashing Nepal by 306 runs at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium on Friday. The emphatic victory, built on centuries from captain Tilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra before a sensational bowling display, marked India A’s biggest-ever win by runs in List A cricket.After posting a formidable 332/9 in their 50 overs, India A bundled Nepal out for a mere 26 in 11.3 overs to seal a dominant victory and make a strong statement in the tournament.India A's biggest List A victories by runsIndia A's 306-run victory over Nepal is their biggest win by runs in List A cricket. Here are the four other major victories identified in the available historical record listings:RankWinning marginOpponentYear1306 runsNepal20262281 runsLeicestershire20183203 runsWest Indies A20184202 runsNetherlands A2006Tilak Varma, Kumar Kushagra power India A to 332Put in to bat, India A suffered a few early setbacks but recovered through a magnificent 206-run partnership between Tilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra. Both batters went on to score centuries, taking the innings away from Nepal.Kushagra smashed 117 off 102 deliveries, including 10 fours and five sixes, while captain Tilak contributed 107 off 113 balls, with six fours and four sixes. Suryansh Shedge provided the late fireworks with an unbeaten 36 off just 14 deliveries, striking four sixes and a boundary to help India A finish at 332/9. For Nepal, Lalit Rajbanshi and Sandeep Lamichhane picked up three wickets apiece.Harshit Rana, Prince Yadav dismantle NepalNepal's chase never got going as India's pace attack made early inroads. Harshit Rana struck in the opening over, dismissing Arjun Kumal for a duck, before Prince Yadav joined the demolition act. Prince removed Deepak Dumre and bowled Basir Ahamad as Nepal slipped to 1/3 inside the first two overs. The wickets continued to tumble as the Indian bowlers maintained relentless pressure.Prince finished with remarkable figures of 5/6 from five overs, while Rana claimed 4/16 in six overs. Shahbaz Ahmed picked up the final wicket, stumping Nandan Yadav for two, as Nepal were dismissed for just 26 in 11.3 overs.Nepal record fifth-lowest total in List A cricketNepal's total of 26 is the fifth-lowest completed innings score in men's List A cricket history. The four lower totals on record are West Indies Under-19's 18 against Barbados in 2007, Saracens Sports Club's 19 against Colts Cricket Club in 2012, Middlesex's 23 against Yorkshire in 1974 and Oman's 24 against Scotland in 2019.The collapse also underlined the scale of India's dominance, with Nepal managing to last only 11.3 overs in their pursuit of 333. The 306-run margin, meanwhile, stands as India A's biggest victory by runs in List A cricket, giving the side a memorable start to their Rising Stars Asia Cup campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: James Anderson: England legend loses Italia T10 league debut for Napoli Knights in first match since Lancashire exit
articles.summary: James Anderson was released by Lancashire at the end of the County Championship season and has joined Surrey in 2027; Anderson is among the players in action for Napoli Knights, a T10 franchise league in Italy
articles.body:
Anderson is co-owner of Napoli Knights, with the 44-year-old's appearance his first since being released by boyhood club Lancashire at the end of the season.

Napoli Knights are one of six teams in the nine-day tournament at Roma Cricket Ground, running until November 28, with Anderson's side restricted to 73-9 after losing the toss and batting first.

Anderson finished nought not out from one delivery faced, scampering a bye from the final ball of the innings, before taking 0-14 from two overs during Rome Gladiators' successful chase.

England's history-making Test bowler conceded just three from a tight opening over of Rome's chase, before being hit down the ground by Singh for a maximum - during an 11-run over - when returning for a second stint later in the innings.

Anthony Mosca fired an unbeaten 45 from 27 deliveries and Jaspreet Singh ended 15 not out from nine, as Rome Gladiators claimed a five-wicket win with two balls remaining.

Wayne Madsen, captaining the Napoli Knights: "It's fantastic to have Jimmy [Anderson] here. He's inspirational to so many of us.

"To be playing with him, and for him to share his knowledge with this group, is amazing. I think, as we've seen, he has still got the skill to go out there and perform at the top level."

Napoli Knights have further matches against Brescia Lions (Saturday), Venice Livewire (Sunday), Milan Icons (Monday) and Bologna Hurricanes (TBC).

Anderson has joined Surrey ahead of the 2027 season in the Rothesay County Championship, having been left "sad" and "quite shocked" by his contract not being extended by Lancashire .

Upon the announcement of his move to the Kia Oval, Anderson said: "It's an honour to join a club like Surrey and I can't wait to start a new chapter in my career. I still feel like I have a lot to offer, taking wickets, trying to help the team win games of cricket.

"I also think that I can bring a lot to the team off the field and help those young players who are looking to develop their skillset and go on and represent their country."

Anderson, who turns 45 in July of next year, will get the opportunity to add to his haul of 1,193 first-class wickets and perhaps more silverware to a glittering CV.

articles.summary: India A captain Tilak Varma was pleased with his side’s performance after their emphatic 306-run win over Nepal in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament,
articles.body: India A captain Tilak Varma was pleased with his side’s performance after their emphatic 306-run win over Nepal in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament, while praising his partnership with Kumar Kushagra.Varma said the pitch was challenging for batting and that the duo wanted to take their partnership deep, knowing it would be difficult for new batters to settle in.“The wicket was slightly challenging. It was not easy to score runs. But the way me and Kumar played, really proud,” he said after the match.The pair added 206 runs for the fourth wicket, with Varma scoring 107 and Kushagra making 117. The skipper revealed they had discussed targeting a total of around 280 before Suryansh Shedge’s late unbeaten 36 off 14 balls lifted India A to 332/9.Varma also praised Harshit Rana’s return from injury, saying it was important for the bowler to deliver such a performance.Looking ahead to the clash against Pakistan A, Varma said India would focus on their basics, adding, “Just another game for us.”India A crush Nepal by 306 runs in Asia Cup Rising Stars openerTilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra hit centuries before Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav demolished Nepal's batting line-up.India A began their Asia Cup Rising Stars 50-over campaign with a commanding 306-run victory over Nepal on Friday, thanks to brilliant centuries from captain Tilak Varma and wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra.After being put in to bat, India A recovered from early setbacks through a 206-run partnership between Varma and Kushagra. Varma scored 107 off 113 balls, while Kushagra smashed 117 off 102 deliveries, helping India A post an imposing 332 for nine. Suryansh Shedge added late momentum with an unbeaten 36 off just 14 balls.Nepal's bowlers Lalit Rajbanshi and Sandeep Lamichhane claimed three wickets each, while Nandan Yadav picked up two.However, Nepal's chase quickly turned into a disaster as India's fast bowlers Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav ripped through their batting line-up. Rana finished with figures of 4/16, while Prince delivered a sensational spell of 5/6, bowling Nepal out for just 26 in 11.3 overs.Nepal lost their first wicket without scoring and slipped to 17 for five by the seventh over.
